answer: Behavioral Fingerprint Divergence Ledger: each identity must submit periodic task traces whose timing and error patterns are hashed into a per-identity profile stored across shards. Duplicate agents share latent signatures, so a canyon of divergence opens between claimed independence and measured behavior, flagging clusters. Flagged clusters forfeit queued rewards and must re-earn standing through a nebula of fresh, unshared tasks. Attackers pay roughly 40 hours of distinct behavioral generation per identity to evade the lagoon of correlated traces.
